title: Phase Relationship Visualizer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: phase difference
leading and lagging
sinusoidal waveform
phasor diagram
AC signals
electrical engineering
description: Interactive MicroSim comparing a reference sinusoid v1(t) = Vm sin(wt) with a phase-shifted sinusoid v2(t) = Vm sin(wt + phi) on a waveform plot and a phasor diagram, with a statement of whether v2 leads or lags v1.

learningObjectives: Compare two sinusoidal signals with different phase relationships and interpret leading/lagging terminology
prerequisites: amplitude, frequency and period of a sinusoid

controls.label: Start / Stop
controls.description: Rotate the phasors in slow motion; starts stopped

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Stop the animation and restore the default phase of 45 degrees

controls.label: Phasor Diagram
controls.description: Show or hide the phasor diagram

assumptions: Both signals have the same amplitude and frequency
Animation runs in slow motion: one 200 ms cycle takes 6 seconds

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Compare waveform and phasor views of the same phase difference
keyQuestions: If v2 leads v1, is the v2 curve shifted to the left or to the right?
How does the angle between the phasors relate to the time between the peaks?
Why do +180 degrees and -180 degrees look identical?
commonMisconceptions: The leading signal is the one drawn further to the right on the time axis
assessmentOpportunities: State the lead/lag relationship and the time shift for a given pair of sinusoids
